title: HOA Manager
description:
The HOA Property Manager is responsible for the day?to?day operations, governance support, vendor oversight, and owner/resident experience across an assigned portfolio of homeowner associations. This role requires strong analytical ability, impeccable attention to detail, and exceptional written and verbal communication skills. The manager serves as the primary liaison among the Board of Directors, unit owners, residents, vendors, and internal teams (Maintenance and Finance), ensuring that association operations comply with governing documents, applicable laws, and company standards while meeting service-level and financial targets.



Key Outcomes (What Success Looks Like):



Accurate, timely Board packets and meeting facilitation with clear minutes and action logs

Portfolio-level adherence to budgets, assessments, and reserve funding plans in partnership with Finance HOA

Proactive maintenance planning and on-time completion of preventive and corrective work with Maintenance HOA

High owner/resident satisfaction, timely resolution of requests, and transparent communications

Clean annual audits, renewed insurance policies, and documented compliance with statutes and governing documents

Up-to-date task/project management in Asana and on-time delivery of recurring HOA cycles and filings



Key Responsibilities:

1) Board & Governance Management

Serve as the primary point of contact for Board members; prepare agendas, Board packets, and management reports for regular and special meetings.

Interpret and apply governing documents (CC&Rs, bylaws, rules) and relevant state statutes in daily operations; coordinate with counsel when required.

Facilitate annual meetings, elections, and owner notices in accordance with legal and governing document requirements.

2) Owner & Resident Relations

Maintain responsive, professional communication with trustees/Board, unit owners, and residents via email, phone, and portal.

Issue timely association-wide notices (policy changes, maintenance schedules, community events, compliance reminders).

Manage and resolve escalations, complaints, architectural review requests (ARC), violations, and hearings within established SLAs.

3) Financial Coordination & Reporting 

Support budget development, reserve study implementation, and monthly variance commentary; review financials for accuracy.

Monitor assessment billing, collections, payment plans, and delinquency follow-up in alignment with collection policies.

Review and approve invoices, code expenses to budgets, and validate vendor work completion prior to payment.

4) Maintenance, Projects & Vendor Management (with Maintenance HOA)

Translate Board priorities into annual maintenance calendars; schedule and track preventive maintenance and inspections.

Open, monitor, and close work orders; ensure scope, SLA, and quality standards are met; maintain accurate asset records.

Bid, negotiate, and manage vendor contracts (landscaping, janitorial, security, pools, roofing, elevators, etc.); perform periodic vendor reviews.

Coordinate capital improvement projects (RFPs, proposals, schedules, owner notifications, punch lists, closeout documents).

5) Information Management & Systems

Keep all HOA Asana projects/boards current with daily updates, dependencies, and follow-ups; maintain recurring tasks and automations.

Process resale and lender questionnaire packages accurately and within service timelines; maintain fee schedules.

Maintain organized digital records (governing docs, minutes, contracts, insurance, warranties, architectural files) in the association’s repository.

6) Team Leadership & Development

Train and onboard new APMs/PMs on processes, systems (Asana, accounting/portal), compliance, and customer service standards.

Promote a collaborative, service-oriented culture aligned with company values; escalate staffing/resource needs to the Unit Head.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

On-time completion rate for recurring HOA tasks and compliance filings

Work-order first-response and average time-to-close (by priority)

Delinquency rate and collections effectiveness; percent of assessments collected

Budget adherence (OPEX/CapEx) and variance accuracy; invoice cycle time

Owner/resident satisfaction score; complaint resolution time

Board satisfaction score (post-meeting surveys) and action-item closure rate

Qualifications:

3+ years of HOA/condo association management or related property management experience

Demonstrated proficiency with task/project management tools (Asana) and owner portals; strong Excel/Google Sheets skills

Exceptional communication (written and verbal), meeting facilitation, and stakeholder management

Strong analytical, organizational, and time-management skills; high attention to detail

Working knowledge of governing documents, meeting procedures, collections, elections, and common HOA statutes

title: Project Coordinator & Business Development Associate
description:
We are looking for a highly organized and proactive Project Coordinator & Business Development Associate to support both project delivery and business growth initiatives.



This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with clients, coordinating multiple projects, conducting research, preparing business materials, and making sure action items are completed on time.



Key Responsibilities



Project Coordination



Coordinate data conversion, data extraction, and system integration projects.



Gather, validate, and document project requirements.



Support client onboarding, data intake, system setup, and project kickoffs.



Track project timelines, milestones, dependencies, action items, and deliverables.



Coordinate with Engineering, Support, Finance, and other internal teams.



Monitor project risks and escalate concerns when needed.



Maintain accurate project records and updates in Jira, CRM, and other tracking tools.



Business Development & Client Support



Join meetings with prospective customers, partners, and stakeholders.



Support lead generation, opportunity research, and market validation.



Research industry trends, competitors, and potential market opportunities.



Assist with customer outreach, customer visits, business trips, and industry events.



Prepare presentations, proposals, executive summaries, reports, and research materials.



Take meeting notes and track follow-up actions.



Support leadership with strategic projects and market expansion initiatives.



Operational & Executive Support



Coordinate between clients, internal teams, partners, and prospective customers.



Provide clear project and opportunity status updates.



Help prepare service orders, agreements, statements of work, and supporting documents.



Coordinate schedules, travel arrangements, logistics, and meeting materials.



Ensure decisions, action items, and follow-ups are properly documented.



Qualifications



Required



Bachelor's degree in Business, Health Informatics, Information Technology, or a related field.



At least 2 years of experience in project coordination, business development, operations, consulting, or a client-facing role.



Strong organization and time-management skills.



Ability to manage several projects and priorities at the same time.



Excellent written and verbal communication skills.



Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills.



Able to work independently and professionally in a fast-paced environment.



Proficient in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel.



Experience using project management or CRM tools.



Preferred



Experience in healthcare, health IT, technology, business development, or market expansion.



Experience with data migration, data extraction, or system integrations.



Familiarity with EMR/EHR workflows.



Basic knowledge of HL7, APIs, file-based exchange, or lab interfaces.



Experience using Jira or CRM systems.



Experience preparing service agreements, statements of work, or project scopes.



Strong research and analytical skills.



Ability to travel to the United States for business engagements when needed.



What We're Looking For



We are looking for someone who is:



Organized and dependable



Client-focused



Strong at follow-through



Comfortable communicating with different stakeholders



Able to turn meetings into clear action items



Comfortable working across both project coordination and business development



Able to prepare professional, executive-ready materials



To apply, please submit your updated resume and include a short introduction highlighting your experience in project coordination, client-facing work, business development, or technology-related projects.

title: Remote Director of Maintenance
description:
Green Ocean Property Management is a growing property-management organization serving residential rental and condominium/HOA portfolios, supported by related service businesses. Our maintenance operation must deliver fast, reliable service while controlling quality, labor, vendor capacity, billing, and client expectations.

Position Summary

The Maintenance Director is the senior functional leader responsible for maintenance performance across Green Ocean Property Management and Pro Services Boston. Reporting to the COO, this person owns service levels, field-team people management, project and coordination workflows, vendor capacity, department financial performance, and the systems required to deliver consistent work.

This is not primarily a dispatcher, technician, or individual project-manager role. The Director leads the maintenance function through clear scorecards, documented processes, direct management of the field team, and defined responsibilities for the Field Operations Specialist, Project Manager / Estimator, and Maintenance Coordination Team. The right person will make maintenance predictable, profitable, and less dependent on the CEO or COO for daily decisions.

Core Outcomes

Reliable service response: Emergency and routine requests are acknowledged, scheduled, and completed against approved service levels.

Controlled backlog: Every open item has a clear owner, status, next action, and escalation path; aged work is reduced and kept within approved limits.

Profitable maintenance delivery: Labor, vendor cost, billing completeness, project margin, and rework are measured and actively managed.

Consistent field quality: Inspections, workmanship standards, documentation, callbacks, and quality reviews are built into the operating process.

Clear people accountability: Field staff receive direct expectations, coaching, performance follow-up, and capacity planning from the Maintenance Director.

Scalable systems: Intake, coordination, project delivery, field execution, vendor management, and owner/property-manager handoffs are documented and repeatable.

Key Responsibilities

Maintenance Operations Leadership

Own the maintenance operating system from request intake through scheduling, field execution, documentation, billing handoff, and closeout.

Set emergency and routine service levels, escalation rules, quality standards, and communication expectations.

Run weekly maintenance operating reviews covering backlog, aging, scheduled work, emergencies, callbacks, staffing, vendor capacity, and financial performance.

Ensure the Maintenance Coordination Team maintains accurate work-order status, scheduling, resident communication, vendor communication, and after-hours handoffs.

Hold the Project Manager / Estimator accountable for scopes, estimates, schedules, project delivery, change control, documentation, and project margins.

Use the Field Operations Specialist for inspections, technical troubleshooting, difficult jobs, field recommendations, and workmanship checks without assigning people-management duties to that role.

Maintain complete, decision-ready records in PropertyMeld, Buildium, approved trackers, and related source systems.

Field Team and People Leadership

Directly manage field staff, including performance expectations, schedules, coaching, attendance, discipline, development, and staffing decisions.

Define required skills, productivity expectations, quality standards, safety practices, and documentation requirements for each field role.

Build labor and vendor capacity plans that match seasonal demand, portfolio growth, emergency coverage, and project commitments.

Identify performance issues early, document expectations, and complete timely follow-up rather than allowing unresolved problems to move upward to the COO.

Create practical onboarding and training plans for field staff, coordinators, estimators, and vendors.

Maintain a span of control that is workable at current headcount and recommend another frontline leadership seat only when workload and staffing data justify it.

Financial and Vendor Leadership

Own the maintenance budget, labor plan, vendor plan, gross-margin review, billing completeness, and material cost controls.

Ensure all billable labor, materials, vendor costs, estimates, approvals, and change orders are documented and handed to Finance on time.

Review vendor performance, pricing, availability, insurance requirements, service quality, and replacement risk.

Partner with Finance to reconcile operational activity with billing, payroll, vendor bills, receivables, and department reporting.

Identify unprofitable work types, repeated callbacks, underbilling, capacity gaps, and process failures, then bring a corrective recommendation to the COO.

Executive and Cross-Functional Leadership

Serve as the COO's accountable leader for maintenance outcomes and risks.

Coordinate with Property Operations, Leasing, Customer Success, On Ramp, Finance, and Systems/Data on handoffs that cross departments.

Convert maintenance data into a short executive do-list with an owner, deadline, metric, and expected business effect.

Build and maintain maintenance playbooks for routine work, emergencies, projects, inspections, vendor use, resident communication, and billing handoff.

Identify risks early and bring a recommendation, not only a problem, to the COO and CEO.

Decision Authority and Boundaries

The Maintenance Director is expected to improve routine maintenance processes, manage staff and vendors, enforce approved controls and deadlines, assign work, resolve routine escalations, and make day-to-day operating decisions within approved policies and budgets.

The Director prepares evidence-based recommendations for executive approval on material unbudgeted commitments, senior hires or terminations, major vendor changes, significant pricing or policy changes, legal or safety matters, and other decisions reserved for the COO or CEO. The Director owns maintenance management and results. The role should not depend on personally performing routine field work or redoing coordinator and project-manager tasks.

Proposed Scorecard

Final targets should be confirmed during the first 30 days after reviewing the current baseline.

Emergency and routine service requests meet approved acknowledgment, scheduling, and completion standards.

Aged work orders remain within approved limits, and every material exception has an owner, next action, and date.

Scheduled work, field productivity, project delivery, and vendor capacity are reported weekly.

Billing documentation, labor, material, estimate, approval, and change-order records are complete and timely.

Callbacks, rework, quality defects, safety issues, and repeated failures are measured and reduced against baseline.

Field staff, the Project Manager / Estimator, Field Operations Specialist, and Maintenance Coordination Team deliver their scorecards without the Director redoing their work.

First 90 Days

First 30 Days - Diagnose and Establish Control

Review the maintenance organization, open roles, direct-report capabilities, workload, current vendors, and existing scorecards.

Assess PropertyMeld data, backlog, aging, emergencies, callbacks, projects, estimates, billing handoffs, margin reporting, and field capacity.

Confirm decision rights for the Field Operations Specialist, Project Manager / Estimator, Maintenance Coordination Team, and field staff.

Identify material client, safety, staffing, vendor, financial, and key-person risks.

Agree with the COO on the final scorecard, reporting cadence, approval limits, and escalation rules.

Days 31-60 - Install the Operating Cadence

Launch one weekly maintenance operating review and one monthly financial and capacity review.

Publish service levels, backlog definitions, escalation rules, quality checks, and communication standards.

Implement direct-report scorecards and regular one-on-ones.

Create the field and vendor capacity plan and assign owners to the highest-risk gaps.

Document the required workflow from intake through billing handoff and closeout.

Days 61-90 - Demonstrate Independent Execution

Run a complete maintenance operating cycle without relying on the CEO or COO for daily decisions.

Show measurable movement in aged backlog, scheduling reliability, quality, billing completeness, and team accountability.

Present a 12-month maintenance improvement plan ranked by business impact, risk, effort, cost, and owner.

Demonstrate that field staff and supporting roles operate against clear metrics and decision rights.

Required Qualifications

Significant progressive experience leading maintenance, facilities, construction service, field operations, or a comparable multi-site service function.

Proven people-management experience, including performance expectations, coaching, discipline, hiring, staffing, and direct accountability for a field team.

Working knowledge of work-order operations, emergency response, estimating, project delivery, vendor management, quality control, and safety practices.

Experience owning a department budget, labor capacity, vendor cost, billing completeness, and operating metrics.

Ability to distinguish technical expertise from people leadership and assign each responsibility to the correct role.

Strong written and verbal communication, follow-through, documentation, and comfort holding staff, vendors, and peers accountable.

Experience with property-management, maintenance-management, scheduling, reporting, and collaboration systems.

Ability to lead a distributed team across field and remote functions.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in residential property management, condominium/HOA management, multifamily operations, or an in-house maintenance business.

Experience with PropertyMeld, Buildium, QuickBooks Online, Google Workspace, and workflow or reporting automation.

Experience improving response time, backlog aging, gross margin, billing completeness, vendor capacity, callbacks, or field productivity with measurable results.

Relevant trade, construction-management, facilities, project-management, or safety qualification.

Benefits and Time Off

Benefits for this full-time role include:

Health insurance: Employer-sponsored health coverage. Eligibility, plan terms, and the employer contribution are governed by the applicable benefit plan and offer letter.

Paid time off (PTO): 15 paid days annually, subject to company policy.

Paid sick time: 5 paid days annually, subject to company policy and applicable law.

Paid holidays, subject to the company holiday calendar.

Leadership Profile

Leads through clear outcomes rather than constant task supervision.

Creates practical controls without unnecessary bureaucracy.

Uses source data before drawing conclusions and distinguishes urgent work from high-value work.

Solves recurring problems through ownership, process, and systems.

Coaches people while holding a firm performance standard.

Communicates bad news early, plainly, and with a recommended next step.

Equal Opportunity

Green Ocean Property Management is committed to providing equal employment opportunities. Employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without unlawful discrimination.



Internal Hiring Note

Because this role directly manages field staff and leads several specialized functions, the hiring process should test people leadership, maintenance operations, financial judgment, vendor management, and the ability to build systems without personally taking over every task. Technical maintenance knowledge without proven people accountability is not sufficient.

Role Performance Metrics

Primary scorecard. Targets are recommended starting points and should be confirmed against the current baseline during the first 30 days.

#

Metric

Target

Measurement source

1

Emergency response control

100% of emergency requests acknowledged within the approved emergency SLA; every missed SLA has a documented cause and corrective action.

PropertyMeld emergency reports and escalation log.

2

Aged backlog control

100% of work older than the approved aging threshold has an owner, next action, and due date; aged backlog improves against the confirmed baseline.

PropertyMeld backlog and aging reports.

3

Schedule reliability

At least 90% of scheduled work is completed by the promised date, excluding documented access, approval, or scope-change delays.

PropertyMeld schedule, completion records, and exception reasons.

4

Billing and margin control

100% of billable labor, materials, vendor costs, approvals, and change orders are documented and submitted on time; department margin is reviewed monthly.

PropertyMeld, time records, vendor bills, Buildium, and finance reporting.

5

Quality and team accountability

Callbacks and rework remain within the approved target; 100% of required scorecards, one-on-ones, reviews, and documented performance follow-ups are completed on time.

Quality reviews, callback log, manager scorecards, and HR records.



Ownership standard: The Director owns these results through field staff, the Project Manager / Estimator, Field Operations Specialist, and Maintenance Coordination Team. Results should reflect independent team performance rather than work the Director personally completed or redid.

title: Director of Finance & People Operations
description:
Green Ocean Property Management is a family-run residential property management company in Boston, Massachusetts. Our family has been in Boston real estate since 1952. We manage 1,000+ condo units, 500+ rental units, and 60+ condominium associations, with 50+ full-time team members across the US and the Philippines. Our clients rate us 4.9 stars on Google.



We're growing, and we're looking for a senior leader to run both our Finance and HR teams.



The Role



You'll report directly to our COO and lead two managers, our Controller and our HR Manager. You'll own the company's financial discipline and its people systems, and make sure both teams deliver accurate, on-time work without needing day-to-day supervision from leadership.



This is NOT a bookkeeping or HR assistant role. It's a manager-of-managers position for someone who has already led finance and HR teams and can turn numbers and people data into clear decisions.



What You'll Do



Finance



Lead the Controller on month-end close, account reconciliations, AR/AP, payroll accounting, and financial reporting

Keep company books (QuickBooks Online) and client/property books (Buildium) clearly separated

Own budgeting, forecasting, a weekly 13-week cash forecast, and monthly variance reviews

Deliver a monthly management report on revenue, margin, expenses, labor, cash, receivables, and risks

Set and enforce internal controls, approval limits, and reconciliation standards

Improve finance dashboards, data quality, and automation

HR & People Operations



Lead the HR Manager and hold the HR team accountable for recruiting, onboarding, performance reviews, retention, and offboarding

Build a workforce plan covering the roles we need, hiring priorities, and compensation cost

Make sure hiring uses role scorecards, structured interviews, and clear pipeline reporting

Track and improve time-to-fill, offer acceptance, 90-day retention, turnover, and review completion

Build compensation ranges, promotion criteria, and career paths

Leadership



Serve as the COO's right hand for finance and HR operations

Turn financial and people data into a short action list with owners and deadlines

Spot problems early and come with a recommendation, not just the problem

Protect confidential employee, payroll, client, and financial information

Requirements



Several years of progressive accounting/finance experience, including month-end close, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and internal controls

Proven experience managing managers (not just individual staff)

Working knowledge of HR operations: recruitment, performance management, payroll and benefits coordination, and employee relations

Experience with US-based companies and US accounting standards

Experience in property management, real estate, or a multi-entity business is a big plus

Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills

Excellent written and spoken English

Comfortable holding managers accountable, respectfully and directly

Available to work US Eastern Time business hours

Reliable internet connection, a laptop/PC, and a working headset and camera

Preferred



CPA, CMA, MBA, or HR certification

Hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online, Buildium, BambooHR, Google Workspace, Asana, or Slack

Experience improving close speed, cash forecasting, collections, or employee retention, with numbers to show for it

What We Offer



$[X,XXX] – $[X,XXX] USD per month

[Benefits: TBD, e.g. paid time off, HMO allowance, paid holidays]

Long-term, stable full-time role with a well-established US company

A true leadership seat reporting directly to the COO

Work from home

How to Apply



Please send the following:



Your updated resume to 

A short cover letter telling us about a finance or HR team you've led, including how many people and what results you achieved

Your Personality Test results link, if you have already taken one

Kindly use the subject line "Director of Finance – [Your Full Name]" so we know you've read the full post. Applications without this subject line will not be reviewed.



Shortlisted applicants will be invited to take an assessment exercise before the interview.



We look forward to hearing from you!

title: Property Manager
description:
Property Manager 

Job Description



Reports to:

Senior PM

Division:

GOPM

Department:

Property Management

Status:

Full-Time

Location and Work Setup:

Remote



Summary:

Green Ocean Property Management (GOPM) is hiring a detail-driven and proactive Property Manager Assistant to support the daily operations of our property management team. In this role, you will be instrumental in maintaining tenant satisfaction, ensuring smooth leasing processes, and coordinating with vendors and internal teams to address property needs.



This is a client-facing, systems-heavy role that requires strong organization, responsiveness, and communication skills. You’ll handle the front lines of tenant communication, assist with maintenance logistics, and contribute to streamlined operational execution — all from a remote environment.

Key Responsibilities:

Tenant Communication & Lease Management

Act as the primary point of contact for tenants — address inquiries, requests, and concerns in a timely, professional manner.

Assist in lease lifecycle management including drafting lease agreements, facilitating renewals, and processing terminations.

Manage rent collection activities, send reminders, escalate late payments, and help enforce payment terms.



Maintenance Coordination

Serve as liaison between tenants, property owners, and vendors.

Schedule and monitor maintenance and repair work orders using internal tracking tools.

Ensure follow-through and resolution of service requests; maintain a high standard of property condition.



Records Management

Maintain up-to-date digital records including leases, inspection reports, rent rolls, and maintenance logs.

Ensure compliance with state and federal property management regulations regarding documentation and tenant interactions.



Tenant Screening & Onboarding

Conduct background checks, verify employment and references for prospective tenants.

Assist in preparing onboarding materials and move-in documentation.



Move-In/Move-Out Support

Assist in the coordination of property inspections for both move-ins and move-outs.

Prepare condition reports and coordinate with vendors for turnover services.

Ensure timely processing of security deposit returns in accordance with regulations.



Reporting & Data Entry

Generate regular operational reports, including:

Occupancy/vacancy rates

Maintenance activity summaries

Rent collection status

Lease expiration schedules

Flag operational risks or trends proactively.



Marketing & Listings Support

Create or update rental listings on platforms such as Zillow,
 Marketplace, and RentRedi.

Coordinate with the leasing team to schedule virtual or in-person property showings.

Monitor listing performance and suggest optimizations.



Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work closely with the property management, leasing, and accounting teams to ensure efficient workflow.

Escalate urgent issues while maintaining alignment with internal processes and SOPs.

Suggest process improvements that enhance tenant experience or team productivity.



Qualifications:

Minimum 2 years experience in property management, real estate operations, or virtual property assistance.

Knowledge of lease administration, rental laws, and maintenance coordination processes.

Ability to multitask across a high volume of properties or tenants.

Excellent communication skills (verbal and written) and professional customer service demeanor.





Technical Proficiency

Strong experience with property management software (e.g., AppFolio, Buildium, RentRedi, or similar).

Proficient in Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Calendar) and Microsoft Office.

Comfortable using remote tools like Slack, Zoom, and project management boards (Asana, Trello).

title: Construction Project Coordinator
description:
We are looking for an experienced and highly organized Construction Project Coordinator to help manage construcConstruction Project Coordinator



tion, renovation, repair, and property improvement projects from start to finish.



Job Summary



The Construction Project Coordinator will oversee daily project coordination, communicate with contractors and vendors, track project progress, and make sure all construction work is completed on time, within budget, and according to company standards.



The ideal candidate has experience in U.S. construction or property management, strong communication skills, and the ability to handle multiple projects at once.



Key Responsibilities



1. Construction Project Coordination



Coordinate construction, renovation, and property improvement projects from planning through completion.



Monitor project timelines, deadlines, budgets, and deliverables.



Work closely with project managers, contractors, vendors, and internal teams.



Track project milestones and provide regular progress updates.



Identify delays and help resolve project issues quickly.



2. Vendor and Contractor Management



Source, screen, and coordinate contractors and subcontractors.



Request and compare construction estimates, bids, and proposals.



Schedule contractors and follow up on work progress.



Verify that contractors complete work according to the approved scope.



Maintain vendor records, contracts, and required insurance documents.



3. Budget and Cost Monitoring



Track project expenses, invoices, and approved budgets.



Review contractor estimates and identify possible cost concerns.



Monitor change orders and additional work requests.



Coordinate invoice approvals and payment requests with the finance team.



4. Documentation and Reporting



Prepare and maintain project schedules, reports, and progress trackers.



Organize construction documents, permits, contracts, and project photos.



Maintain accurate records of project communication and decisions.



Provide daily or weekly updates to management.



Ensure project information is updated in company systems.



5. Quality Control and Project Completion



Coordinate remote project inspections using photos, videos, and reports from on-site teams.



Track punch lists and outstanding construction issues.



Follow up on incomplete or delayed work.



Help confirm that completed work meets the approved scope and quality standards.



Coordinate final project closeout and documentation.



Qualifications

title: Virtual Sales Manager - American Medspa Bookings
description:
VIRTUAL SALES MANAGER – APPOINTMENT SETTING TEAM (REMOTE)



Location: Philippines (Remote)



Industry: U.S. Medical Spa & Health and Wellness



Position: Virtual Sales Manager / Appointment Setting Manager



Schedule: U.S. Eastern Time (EST/EDT)



Compensation: Competitive base pay + performance-based bonuses



ABOUT THE POSITION



We are a growing medical spa and health and wellness company based in the United States, seeking an experienced, results-driven Virtual Sales Manager to lead our remote appointment-setting team.



You will be responsible for managing multiple Philippines-based Virtual Assistants (VAs) who contact prospective clients, follow up with leads, and schedule appointments for our U.S. locations.



This is a hands-on leadership position. We are looking for someone who knows how to motivate salespeople, improve conversion rates, identify performance problems, and hold team members accountable for their results.



Your primary responsibility is to ensure our appointment setters are consistently converting leads into qualified appointments that actually show up.



We are not looking for someone who simply monitors attendance or distributes tasks. We need a proactive manager who takes ownership of their team's performance and continuously finds ways to improve results.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



1. Sales Team Management



- Manage, supervise, and support multiple remote appointment-setting VAs.

- Monitor daily attendance, punctuality, productivity, and individual performance.

- Ensure team members consistently meet established call, follow-up, and appointment-booking goals.

- Conduct regular team meetings and individual performance reviews.

- Identify underperforming employees and implement improvement plans.

- Maintain a positive, competitive, and results-oriented team culture.



2. Sales Coaching & Development



- Review recorded calls and evaluate appointment setters' communication and sales skills.

- Provide direct, actionable feedback to improve conversations and conversion rates.

- Train employees on objection handling, appointment setting, lead qualification, and effective follow-up.

- Conduct role-playing exercises and ongoing sales training.

- Identify successful sales strategies and implement them across the team.

- Help onboard and train new appointment setters.



3. Performance Tracking & Reporting



- Monitor individual and team performance using our CRM and reporting tools.

- Track important KPIs, including outbound calls, call connection rates, appointments booked, lead-to-appointment conversion rates, appointment show rates, and appointments resulting in purchases.

- Prepare daily performance summaries and communicate results to company leadership.

- Identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement.

- Ensure all team members maintain accurate CRM records.



4. Lead Management & Appointment Quality



- Ensure leads are contacted promptly and followed up with consistently.

- Monitor lead distribution and make sure opportunities are not being overlooked.

- Ensure appointment setters follow approved scripts, procedures, and scheduling guidelines.

- Improve appointment quality by ensuring clients understand the purpose of their visits and are prepared to attend.

- Work to reduce no-shows and improve overall appointment attendance.

- Coordinate with the U.S. team regarding scheduling issues, client feedback, and operational changes.



5. Process Improvement & Accountability



- Evaluate current appointment-setting systems and recommend improvements.

- Develop and maintain training materials, sales scripts, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

- Identify inefficiencies and implement solutions without needing constant direction.

- Hold employees accountable to performance standards and company policies.

- Support hiring, interviewing, onboarding, and evaluating new team members as needed.



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS



- Previous experience managing a remote sales, telemarketing, call center, or appointment-setting team.

- Proven ability to coach sales representatives and improve measurable performance.

- Strong understanding of outbound calling, lead follow-up, objection handling, and appointment-setting techniques.

- Excellent spoken and written English.

- Strong leadership, communication, and conflict-resolution skills.

- Experience working with American customers or U.S.-based businesses.

- Comfortable tracking KPIs, analyzing performance data, and preparing reports.

- Experience using CRM software and call monitoring systems.

- Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple employees simultaneously.

- Reliable internet connection, professional workspace, and availability during assigned U.S. business hours.



PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS



- Experience managing Philippines-based appointment setters serving U.S. businesses.

- Experience with GoHighLevel (GHL) or similar CRM platforms.

- Previous experience in medical spas, aesthetics, wellness clinics, or other appointment-based businesses.

- Experience creating sales scripts, training programs, and performance improvement plans.

- Familiarity with commission-based sales compensation structures.

- Experience managing teams that handle high volumes of inbound and outbound leads.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE



A successful manager in this position will:



- Consistently improve appointment-booking and appointment-attendance rates.

- Maintain a motivated, reliable, and productive sales team.

- Identify performance problems early and take corrective action.

- Ensure leads receive timely, consistent follow-up.

- Improve sales results through coaching, training, and process improvements.

- Provide leadership with clear, accurate reporting.

- Take ownership of the team's results without requiring constant supervision.



We value results, initiative, consistency, and accountability.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



The ideal candidate is a natural leader with a strong sales background who understands that managing a team means more than checking whether employees are working.



You should be someone who listens to calls, studies performance data, coaches employees, and actively looks for ways to increase the number of qualified appointments booked and attended.



We want someone who treats the performance of the sales team as their personal responsibility and takes pride in building a high-performing operation.



HOW TO APPLY



Please submit your resume along with answers to the following questions:



1. How many sales or appointment-setting employees have you directly managed at one time?

2. What KPIs did you use to measure their performance?

3. Describe a situation where you improved an underperforming sales team's results. What specifically did you change, and what were the results?

4. What experience do you have with GoHighLevel?

5. How would you handle an appointment setter who consistently makes calls but books very few appointments?

6. Are you comfortable working hours that align with U.S. Eastern Time?



We are looking for someone interested in a long-term position with the opportunity to grow as our company expands.

title: AI VIDEO EDITOR & MOTION GRAPHICS ARTIST
description:
👋 ABOUT US



We're two young entrepreneurs starting a faceless YouTube channel for a US audience, with story-driven, documentary-style videos.



We're just getting started, so this is the perfect moment to join. We're looking for someone who wants to grow with us. As our channel grows, we'd love to make you our Head Editor, with more responsibility, more videos and a higher rate. We're looking for a long-term partner, not a one-time freelancer.



⭐ THE QUALITY WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Our benchmark is the production level of channels like Magnates Media, for example this video:





We don't want to copy their style, but we're aiming for that level of quality. What matters most to us:



• The visuals explain the story

Every important sentence in the voice-over is supported by a visual that shows what is being said. If the narrator says a company lost $50 million, the viewer sees a bank balance dropping. If something grows from 20,000 to 1 million, the viewer sees a counter racing up.



• No random stock footage

No generic clips that have nothing to do with what's being said.



• Movement and rhythm

Animated text, numbers, charts, maps and smooth transitions, timed precisely to the voice-over.



• Visually attractive

Cinematic, modern and consistent, so viewers keep watching from start to finish.



🛠️ WHAT YOU'LL DO



• Turn our script into a complete 8–10 minute video

• Create the voice-over: a deep, calm, professional documentary voice (an AI voice is fine, as long as it has a commercial license)

• Create motion graphics: animated numbers, charts, counters, text and maps

• Select and edit licensed footage, music and sound effects

• Add subtitles

• Deliver the final video in 1080p (4K is a plus) plus the project files





📦 WHAT WE PROVIDE



• Full script with timestamps and visual notes

• Clear feedback and fast communication



✅ REQUIREMENTS



• A strong portfolio with documentary, explainer or storytelling videos

• Strong motion graphics skills

• Any software or tools are fine, as long as the result meets our quality standard

• Only licensed footage, music, sound effects and voices (no copyrighted material)

• Good written English and reliable communication



➕ NICE TO HAVE



• Experience with documentary or storytelling YouTube channels

description:
I’m Gloria Carmona, Director of the Estates Division at Compass in Los Angeles. I represent luxury buyers and sellers, and I run my business on one principle: we have a process for everything, and we follow it every single time.



I’m looking for one person to become the operational backbone of my business. This is not a task list. It’s a long-term role for someone who loves order, protects the details, and thinks about how to make the business grow.



What you’ll own



Client process: run my buyer and seller systems from first contact to closing and beyond. Every checklist, every step, every time.

Systems building: help document and refine my processes into written procedures, templates and checklists. If a process doesn’t exist yet, you build it.

Calendar & appointments: manage my schedule, showings, consultations and follow-ups.

Client care: keep my CRM clean, track birthdays, anniversaries and home anniversaries, and keep past clients feeling remembered.

Geographic farm: run my bimonthly mailer program, including postcards, letters, event invitations, coordination and deadlines.

Marketing: Canva designs, social media support for growth and recognition. All newsletters and listing marketing for properties can be coordinating with the Compass marketing team.

Events: coordinate client events remotely: vendors, flyers, invitations, timelines and follow-up.

Growth ideas: I want your opinion. Every month you’ll bring me at least one idea to grow the business, improve a process or serve clients better.



Who you are



Extremely organized. You notice when something is out of place and you fix it before anyone asks.

You follow a process exactly, and you also tell me when it can be better.

Excellent written English. My clients are high-net-worth, and everything we send reflects that.

2+ years as an executive assistant, real estate VA or marketing coordinator.

Strong in Canva, Google Workspace and Compass CRM 

Real estate experience is a must, Spanish is a bonus.



Details



Part Time with high possibility of becoming full time,  with at least [4] hours overlapping Pacific Time ([10am–2pm PT])

Pay: $5 to $10 per hour based on experience, with raises tied to performance

Long-term position. I invest in people who invest in the business.



How to apply (read carefully)



Begin your application with the words “Every single time.”

In 3–5 sentences, describe a process you created or improved and what changed because of it.

Give me one idea for how a luxury real estate agent could stay top-of-mind with past clients.

Attach a short Loom or video (2 minutes max) introducing yourself.



Applications that don’t follow these instructions won’t be reviewed. In this role, following the process is the job, and creating a better process is the job.

title: Accounting Director ($5k/Month, PTO, 13th Month)
description:
Director of Client Accounting Services

Location: Remote, any country

Pay: $5,000 USD a month

Schedule: Full time. Core hours 9am to 2pm US Eastern on working days.

Reports to: Senior Director, Operations. Works directly with the owner.



You are the person other accountants bring the problem to. The difference nobody can find. The intercompany balance that will not tie. The client who has run out of patience. You fix it, and then someone above you, who often knows less about it than you do, d
 what happens next. This job gives you the decisions.



About Monterra

Monterra is a US accounting and tax firm. We have served business owners since 1991. Most of our clients own many businesses at once: groups with ten, twenty or more locations, each its own company, with numbers that have to tie across all of them.



Specialists. We have built the firm around owners of many businesses, so you spend your time on hard, interesting books instead of a long tail of one-off files.



Thirty-five years, and growing. New multi-location groups signed with us this fall, and not one client has left us in the past year.

We build our own tools. We wrote our own tax planning software, and we are rebuilding accounting the same way.



Remote by design. The whole firm works remotely. You will not be the one person on a different clock in an office that forgot you exist.



The role

We have more good clients than we have people to serve them, so we are hiring one person to run our whole client accounting department: the team, the standards, the final review and the numbers. There is no partner to wait on. When you see a better way to run it, you have the authority to change it. We are rebuilding the department around automation, and you d
 what gets automated and write the procedure the team follows once it works.



What you will own

The team: workloads, deadlines, coaching, hiring and performance for every accountant, in-house and outsourced

Final technical review of every close and financial statement before it reaches a client

One written method for every recurring task, plus a quality control program with monthly sample checks and an error log

Hours against benchmark and realization for every client, reported to leadership on one page each month

Onboarding each new client to a first clean close, and the client call when something goes wrong

The automation rebuild, starting with bank reconciliation matching, and a second-in-command who can run the department without you



Requirements

We judge what you have done, not how long you did it. You must be able to show us:

A team of accountants you ran for clients, and what changed because you ran it: closes that came in on time and errors that went down

Your record as the final reviewer on other accountants' work: closes and financial statements for multi-entity groups

A bank reconciliation you did yourself in the last twelve months

A procedure you wrote that a team actually follows

An outsourced or remote team you held to a standard, with numbers to prove it

English strong enough to explain a set of financial statements, or a mistake in them, to a US business owner on a live call



Nice to have

Franchise accounting, including 13-period calendars

Thomson Reuters Accounting CS

Accounting work you automated, and the hours it saved

You do not need a degree, a licence, a particular title or a set number of years.



Pay and perks

$6,000 to $7,000 USD a month, paid in US dollars wherever you live

Annual bonus tied to your team's performance.

Work from anywhere. Fully remote, in any country.

Run your own day outside the core hours.

A short line to the top. Your proposals go to the Senior Director, Operations and the owner, and you get an answer.

Your own bench. You choose and develop the person who will be your number two.

Paid time off. Two weeks to start, plus all US holidays and the public holidays where you live.



Your first year

First 30 days: You learn every client and meet every accountant. You start on the bank reconciliations for our largest client group.

By day 90: The buck stops with you on every client close and you run the weekly workload review. Your review standard and onboarding checklists are in use. Your first monthly report is sent.

By month 6: Every recurring task has one written method. Monthly quality checks are running. Our outsourced partner is held to the hours and quality we agreed, with data.

By month 9: You own the department. At least one automated workflow is live under your procedures. Someone on your team can run the department for two weeks while you are away.



How we hire

We do not screen on job titles or count your years. We ask what you did, with numbers, and who can confirm it.

Application. About 35 minutes. Three short accounting tests and questions about your results. No cover letter.

Work test one. A month-end close review, a bank reconciliation and a written procedure, built from the work you would own here. About 2.5 hours.

Work test two. Your first weeks in the seat, in one data pack. About 2.5 hours.

Interview with the owner. We contact your references after the interview, not before.

Every application gets a reply. You will never wait weeks in silence wondering whether anyone read your work.



How to apply

Apply here: 
. There is one seat.
